clue.text: To take a look at ladies' make-up can result in shock!

parts.note: to scan is to take a quick look at something

indicators.note: the make-up of something is how it is put together, so these letters are composed afresh

explanation.surface: Seeing women putting on cosmetics might cause outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' reads as cosmetics on the ladies, but it is the signal to rearrange; 'can result in' merely links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To scandalise someone is to outrage or appal them, a synonym for shocking them.

parts.note: reads like praise for a forward-thinking leader, but means a prophet who literally sees what is to come

explanation.definitionFit: A prophet or clairvoyant claims to see the future, so is a man of vision in the literal sense.

clue.text: Take turns, and so maybe aren't late

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Swap shifts with someone, and then perhaps you won't be tardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals an anagram of AREN'T LATE (the apostrophe is ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to do things by turns, one after the other.

explanation.surface: An artist portrays someone who looks tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture that is drawn has been depicted in pencil; a face that is drawn looks tired and haggard.

clue.text: Support a friend in proper fashion

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
an ally is a friend or partner

explanation.surface: Backing a companion in the correct manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting lawfully means acting within the rules, in a proper and permitted way.

parts.note: to set something is to plant it, as seedlings are set out
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A garden centre hands over a shrub at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to liberate or release them from captivity.

definitions.meaning: the pick of the bunch is the best thing on offer
a stone fruit, purple or yellow

explanation.surface: An instruction to harvest something from an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: The choicest job or prize is called a plum, just like the pick of the bunch; it is also a common stone fruit.

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A customer asks the barman for a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a request at a bar but means rearrange LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a drink served by the pint.

clue.text: The girl offered a hand when prepared to work

definitions.text: The girl offered a hand when prepared to work

parts.words: The girl offered a hand when prepared to work
parts.note: sounds like a woman agreeing to help, but describes someone whose work begins once a client's hand is held out to her

explanation.definitionFit: A beautician who tends fingernails works on a hand presented to her by the customer.

parts.note: violinists are players, and cheats who fiddle the books are unscrupulous, so one word covers both

explanation.definitionFit: A violinist is a player of the fiddle, and to fiddle is also to swindle or cheat.

clue.text: In Essex tradesmen expect to get more

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers in an English county anticipate earning a bigger income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sounds like a location in the county but tells you the answer sits inside 'Essex tradesmen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, something on top of what you have.

explanation.surface: Someone is doing well in life even though they are past their youth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both making headway in life and growing elderly.

parts.note: a disputatious person is one who argues, and Cambridge gives a special title to its top mathematics graduates

explanation.walkthrough: At Cambridge University a student awarded first-class honours in mathematics is given this title.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means one who argues, and is also the Cambridge title for a first-class mathematics graduate.

clue.text: Serve endless rice in the Greek way

parts.note: to do someone is to serve them, as a barber does a customer

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word rice is dropped

explanation.surface: A waiter dishes up a short helping of rice in Hellenic style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the last letter of RICE to give RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of ancient Greek architecture, and a dialect of ancient Greece.

parts.note: sounds like a cheer for breaking a best time, but means a chart recording each pulse of the heart

explanation.definitionFit: A medical trace of heartbeats is a recording of the heart's rhythm.

clue.text: Cunning in no matter what form of lawlessness

indicators.note: in says one word goes inside the other

parts.note: any, as in any one at all
arch means sly or knowing

explanation.surface: Crafty behaviour in any shape amounts to disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'Cunning' is the adjective arch, as in an arch smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is a state with no government or order, a kind of chaos.

parts.note: cash is money in hand
mere means nothing more than, only

explanation.surface: A cynic insists that wealth is all that matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine wool fabric, a cloth woven from goat hair.

clue.text: Person given a free choice, being a prince

definitions.meaning: a voter, who chooses freely at the ballot box
a German prince who had a vote in choosing the Holy Roman Emperor

explanation.surface: A royal is allowed to choose as he likes.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter chooses a candidate; historically the German princes who chose the Emperor bore this title.

parts.note: sounds like a rebel's confession, but means a gate that rotates to let people in one at a time

explanation.definitionFit: A rotating gate at a stadium or station admits people as it revolves.

clue.text: Far out from land, but seeing a point speed back

indicators.note: back means the whole of the phrase a point speed is read from end to start

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor sees a headland and hurries back while well offshore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole of A + E + SPEED to give DEEPSEA; the 'point' is a compass point, not a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocean waters far beyond the coast are the deep ones, well away from shore.

clue.text: An Italian writer given musical instruction

parts.note: taken as written
Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A poet from Italy is handed some guidance on music.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a tempo marking telling players to go at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Maintains stress may be caused by article

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else when reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone claims that tension can be brought on by a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' is the anagram signal; 'article' is the grammatical one, not a news story, and 'caused by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to state it firmly, insisting it is true.

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A feline with nine lives might be getting on a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals an anagram of CAT-NINE (the hyphen is ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancient dates from long ago, extremely aged.

clue.text: Reading poetry with some hesitation in the theatre

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An actor falters while reciting verse on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece and Rome an odeum was a building for musical and poetic performances, a kind of playhouse.

clue.text: A quarter come down for the big game

parts.note: east is one of the four quarters of the compass
to land is to come down to earth

explanation.surface: A fraction of a group descends to watch a major match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big game' suggests a sporting fixture, but it is the hunter's term for large wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope hunted as big game.

explanation.surface: Lobbying for a cut in something.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing removes creases, so read playfully as de-crease; a decrease is also a fall in amount.

definitions.meaning: a bird of prey soaring at height
a score of two under par for a hole

explanation.surface: A soaring bird is spotted over the fairways.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird of prey soars high, and golfers use the same word for a hole completed two strokes under par.

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A handful of garments are laid out to wear beneath clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal; British vests are worn under a shirt, unlike the American waistcoat sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest in British use is a sleeveless undershirt worn beneath a shirt.

clue.text: Give changed order to back and a row will follow

indicators.note: will follow says the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row or line, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Instructions to reshuffle so that the back comes first and the line comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in a new sequence is to reorganise them.

clue.text: Deceptive aspect of an old French town

definitions.meaning: ..., a town in northern France, seat of the dukes of ...

explanation.surface: A French place that is not what it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the guise of means under a false appearance; Guise is also a historic town in Picardy.

parts.note: mad means furious
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: A calm intellectual who is nonetheless seething.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but means the head (first letter) of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made has been put together or created, the sense of composed as in a song composed by someone.

definitions.meaning: a village or colony where people have settled

explanation.surface: A village shows its determination.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal ending a dispute is one sense, and a place where people have made their homes is the other.
